A Labyrinth of Ash and Stone

Carved into the jagged eastern cliffs of the Blasted Lands, the winding path and caverns of Serpent's Coil wind past ruined orcish huts that date back to the First and Second Wars. Rather than simple beasts, the tunnels harbor cabals of Shadowsworn cultists and practitioners of dark arts drawn to the residual demonic energies permeating the red wastes. Deep within its twisting hollows, odd figures pursue private obsessions far from the watchful eyes of Nethergarde Keep.

The caverns have long served as a staging ground for Archmage Allistarj's cultists, who revere demonic lords and experiment with sinister artifacts like the Amulet of Allistarj. Even when their master's grasp wavers, loyal Shadowsworn zealots continue to patrol the cave turns, maintaining rituals in Kirith the Damned's service while hiding behind scorched barricades.

The Sewers are a sprawling subterranean drainage network that provides a secondary entrance directly into the Undercity. Cutting beneath the hills west of the ruined palace of Lordaeron, this conduit allows bat handlers and stealthy travelers to bypass the precarious elevators leading down from the throne room.

Before the plague wiped out Lordaeron, these stone culverts served as the mundane sewer lines draining the royal capital. In the hands of Sylvanas Windrunner's Forsaken, however, the runoff tunnels have been integrated into the Undercity's outer defenses. Emerging west of the surface ruins near a contested Scarlet Watchtower in Tirisfal Glades, the passage provides a level, direct slope inside. Forsaken bat handlers use this cavernous conduit to fly riders swiftly into the subterranean rings, avoiding the sluggish cage lifts entirely. Because it circumvents the heavily fortified surface courtyards, it remains a dangerous vulnerability that hostile infiltrators constantly seek to exploit.

Shadow Hold is a sprawling subterranean complex hidden within the blighted canyon of Jaedenar in western Felwood. Once a sacred night elf barrow den, it has been seized and desecrated by the Shadow Council to serve as their primary bastion on Kalimdor.

Beneath the corrupted red earth of Jaedenar lies Shadow Hold, a vast underground labyrinth carved out of what was once an ancient night elf barrow den. Where sleeping druids once rested to tend the Emerald Dream, dark warlocks and demonic servitors now stalk twisted corridors illuminated by fel fire. At its deepest tiers, the cult commands a formidable force under the dreadlord Lord Banehollow, Prince Xavalis, and Shadow Lord Fel'dan, making it the supreme seat of demonic influence in the region.

The Shadow Council uses the caverns to coordinate their corruption of Felwood and conduct brutal interrogations. Alliance scouts, including the night elf Arko'narin Starshade and the human paladin Trey Lightforge, fell into cultist hands deep inside the hold. While Arko'narin survived through timely rescue, Trey was tortured to death by the cult's torturers, his spirit briefly twisted into malice before being laid to rest. The Emerald Circle and local shamans work constantly to pierce the dark barriers shielding the hold in hopes of striking down its demonic masters.

Perched on a rugged bluff overlooking Pyrewood Village in southern Silverpine Forest, Shadowfang Keep is the dark lair of the mad Archmage Arugal and his feral worgen. Formerly known as Silverlaine Keep, the fortress fell to ravenous wolf-beasts summoned during the Third War, leaving its ancient halls haunted by the slain nobility and crawling with lupine horrors.

Before the Third War, this towering fortress was called Silverlaine Keep, the ancestral seat of Baron Silverlaine and the center of authority for nearby Pyrewood Village. When the Scourge swept through Lordaeron, desperate wizards sought forbidden means to stem the undead tide. Relying on the dimensional research of the Dalaran mage Ur, the Archmage Arugal summoned the extra-dimensional worgen into Azeroth. The savage beasts tore through the Scourge, but quickly spiraled out of control. Rampaging across southern Silverpine, the pack besieged the stronghold, slaughtering Baron Silverlaine, his family, and Commander Springvale's defenders. Guilt and grief shattered Arugal's sanity; rather than flee, he claimed the fortress, renaming it Shadowfang Keep and adopting the monstrous predators as his 'children.'

Today, Shadowfang Keep serves as the epicenter of a growing wolf curse that plagues Silverpine Forest. Arugal dwells in the highest observatory, flanked by his ravenous worgen—including the Moonrage and Shadowfang packs—and sinister beasts like his massive pet wolf, Fenrus. Below his sanctum, the restless ghosts of the keep's former lords, such as Baron Silverlaine and Commander Springvale, remain trapped in torment, cursed to endlessly defend the halls they failed to protect in life. From atop these walls, Arugal extends his insidious influence down into Pyrewood Village and the surrounding woodlands, posing a dire threat to the neighboring Forsaken who seek to purge the forest of his madness.

Shadowglen is a secluded, twilit vale nestled within the northeastern boughs of Teldrassil. Dominated by the great barrow-tree Aldrassil, it serves as the safe haven where young night elves take their first steps into service before journeying out into the wider world.

Tucked away in the northeastern canopy of Teldrassil, Shadowglen is ringed by high ridges that shelter it from the rest of the world. Bathed in eternal dusk, the vale centers on Aldrassil, a massive barrow-tree whose hollowed trunk houses elders, priestesses, and mentors for young night elves beginning their training. The only route out of the valley leads south through a narrow mountain pass toward Starbreeze Village and Dolanaar, making Shadowglen one of the most naturally fortified and peaceful sanctuaries on the World Tree.

Despite its tranquil seclusion, Shadowglen is not entirely free from danger. In the extreme northwest lies Shadowthread Cave, a dark cavern infested with venomous spiders that constantly threaten the tranquil glade. Even on the pristine branches of Teldrassil, vigilance is required, and fledgling defenders are tasked with driving back the encroaching vermin and untamed wildlife before venturing into the broader expanse of the boughs beyond.

Shadowprey Village is a remote Horde fishing settlement built along the rocky southern coast of Sar'theris Strand in Desolace. Populated largely by Darkspear troll fishermen and supported by tauren service keepers, it acts as a critical coastal outpost and trade lifeline amidst a barren wasteland.

Tucked against the cliffs of southern Desolace, Shadowprey Village offers safe harbor in a region notorious for centaur clans and desolate wastes. The settlement is primarily an encampment of troll fishermen whose hauls sustain not only their own village but also inland outposts like Ghost Walker Post. Despite the rough shoreline, towering wooden piers reach out into the ocean, allowing local anglers to brave deep waters and dive for shellfish among the submerged wreckage dotting Sar'theris Strand.

Maintaining a frontier port in Desolace is fraught with danger. Beyond the inland threat of marauding centaur, the ocean itself tests the village's survival. Local waters are haunted by ravenous sea life—notably the monstrous orca Blubbergut, who gorges on the fish stocks—and encroachment from violent lobstrok along the southern banks. Tauren allies, including Taiga Wisemane and the keepers of the inn and wind rider roost, help shore up defenses and keep trade routes open across Kalimdor.

The shrine shares its name with two legendary figures of kaldorei history: Jarod Shadowsong, the reluctant general who led the night elf resistance during the War of the Ancients, and his sister Maiev, the unrelenting warden of Illidan Stormrage. Shadowthread Cave is a damp cavern carved into the northwest cliffs of Shadowglen on Teldrassil. Traditionally inhabited by indigenous Webwood spiders, the cave has recently turned dangerously aggressive under the dominion of their broodmother, Githyiss the Vile.

Tucked away in the shaded perimeter of Shadowglen, Shadowthread Cave has long served as a natural lair for Teldrassil's giant spiders. In earlier years, these arachnids coexisted quietly alongside the nascent boughs of the World Tree. Recently, however, their temperament has turned fiercely territorial. Thick layers of webwood silk now choke the stone corridors, and the aggressive nature of the brood poses an immediate hazard to young kaldorei taking their first steps beyond Aldrassil.

The primary menace lurking deep within the cave's darkest recesses is Githyiss the Vile, a monstrous broodmother whose ferocity far outstrips the common webwood crawlers. The Shady Rest Inn was once a welcoming human-built waystation sitting just off the road between the Barrens and Theramore Isle. The tragedy left the innkeeper shattered and sparked tension across the marsh as investigators sift through the wreckage for clues.

That ended when the inn was abruptly razed to the ground in a devastating fire. Innkeeper James Hyal managed to survive the inferno, but the blaze claimed the lives of his wife and child. Traumatized and grief-stricken, Hyal was left with nothing as the ruins became an active crime scene, drawing scrutiny from Theramore authorities desperate to identify who ignited the flames.
